prompt: The system $kx + 3y = 9$ and $2x + y = 5$ has no solution. What is the value of $k$?
hint: No solution means the lines are parallel — equal slopes.

hints.text: No solution means the lines are parallel — equal slopes.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try it on a known pair: $y = 3x + 1$ and $y = 3x + 7$ never meet, because the slopes match and the intercepts do not. Setting the two slopes equal is the whole technique.
The first line has slope $-\dfrac{k}{3}$ and the second has slope $-2$.

learningObjective: Find the parameter that makes a system inconsistent.
explanation: For $Ax + By = C$ the slope is $-A/B$. The first line has slope $-k/3$; the second has slope $-2/1 = -2$.
Parallel lines have equal slopes: $-\dfrac{k}{3} = -2$, so $k = 6$.
Check that they are genuinely parallel rather than identical: with $k = 6$ the first is $6x + 3y = 9$, or $2x + y = 3$ — same slope as $2x + y = 5$ but a different constant, so they never meet ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Scale to match, then compare
steps: For no solution the $x$ and $y$ coefficients must match the first equation while the constants differ.
Matching $6x$ requires $k = 6$, and the constants $9$ and $15$ do differ — confirming no solution rather than infinitely many.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: A sign slip in the slope comparison hands you k = −6, and stopping early can hand you the infinitely-many case by accident.
After finding k, always compare the constants too: same slope with the SAME constant is one line, not parallel lines.
